# Company 093 — Consent & Preference Management Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:093`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:093`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-093-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer consent capture, communication or downstream data-processing change.

## Business identity
Purpose: maintain provable user/customer consent and communication/data preferences across channels, purposes, systems and jurisdictions, then synchronize those choices to downstream enforcement points.

## Product tree
Consent Ledger; Preference Center; Web/Cookie Consent; Mobile SDK; Email/SMS/Phone/Push Preferences; Marketing/Analytics/Advertising Consent; Data Sharing/Profiling/AI Processing Consent; Personalization/Location/Research Consent; Purpose Registry; Consent Receipt; Withdrawal/Reconsent; Expiration/Refresh; Age/Parental Consent Workflow; Regional Policy Packs; Downstream Sync/Enforcement; Conflict Detector; Audit/Proof; API/SDK/Widgets; Enterprise/Private Deployment; OEM/Embedded Consent Service.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: subject/account identity, purpose, data category, channel, controller/company, jurisdiction, policy/text version, lawful/consent basis reference, choice, source, timestamp, proof, expiry, withdrawal, parent/guardian relation, downstream processors, sync state and evidence.
Customers: SaaS, ecommerce, apps, marketplaces, media, enterprises, privacy/marketing teams, customer-data platforms and developers.
Verticals: consumer apps, commerce, marketing, analytics, health administrative communications, education/minors, finance-adjacent communications and AI/personalization products.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may interpret preference language and detect conflicts; deterministic policy must enforce purpose/channel decisions. Architecture: subject identity, purpose/data taxonomy, versioned consent ledger, policy/jurisdiction packs, preference UI/widget, downstream processor graph, sync/outbox, receipt/proof service, conflict engine and audit.

## Agent tree
Consent Intake Agent; Preference Agent; Policy Mapping Agent; Conflict Agent; Reconsent/Expiry Agent; Downstream Sync Agent; Processor Inventory Agent; Proof/Evidence Agent; Privacy QA Agent.

## Deterministic services
Choice recording; versioned text hash; effective/expiry; withdrawal precedence; channel/purpose checks; parental/guardian relation state; synchronization/retry; processor mapping; signed receipts; audit.

## Workflow tree
Present exact purpose/text/version → capture authenticated/allowed choice → issue receipt → store immutable history/current effective state → propagate to downstream systems → verify sync → runtime processing/communication checks consult current preference → withdrawal immediately supersedes prior grant → reconsent/expiry workflows as policy requires → evidence/reporting.

## Integrations / API / data
Web/mobile apps, CRM/CDP, email/SMS/push, analytics/ad systems, AI/personalization, data warehouses, preference centers and privacy/DSAR systems. Data: subjects, purposes, policies/text versions, choices, receipts, processor mappings and sync state.

## Monetization / distribution
MAU/profiles, consent events, domains/apps, processors/connectors, seats, enterprise/private, API/SDK and policy packs. Distribution through privacy/CDP/marketing/dev ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Consent itself is sensitive evidence. No dark patterns, no fabricated consent, withdrawal must propagate, child/parent rules explicit, purpose limitation, data minimization, jurisdiction awareness and immutable proof. Product does not substitute for legal advice.

## Failure / edge cases
Anonymous-to-authenticated merge, shared household, duplicate profiles, offline mobile consent, policy text changed, processor sync failed, consent withdrawn during queued campaign, minors aging into adult status, conflicting account/channel preferences, global vs purpose-specific opt-out.

## Scale / overlap
Preference center → enterprise consent graph → cross-system preference enforcement. Overlap #47 DSAR, #78 retention, #84 deliverability. #093 owns current consent/preference state and proof.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** purpose/action metadata, subject identity, versioned owner/user decisions, effective/expiry/supersession, downstream enforcement and proof.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center owner preferences/rules already need explicit scope/version/supersession; future customer data should use the same conceptual pattern without mixing identities.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer subject/purpose/processor registry and consent synchronization.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** widgets/SDK/customer systems/legal packs/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** massive regional processor graph.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: ledger/preference/web/mobile/channels/marketing/analytics/sharing/AI/location/purpose/receipts/withdraw/reconsent/age/regional/sync/API.
2. Feature Tree: subject/purpose/data/channel/controller/jurisdiction/text version/choice/source/time/proof/expiry/withdraw/processor/sync.
3. Customer Tree: SaaS/commerce/apps/marketplace/media/enterprise/privacy/marketing/CDP/dev.
4. Vertical Tree: consumer/commerce/marketing/analytics/health admin/education/minors/finance comms/AI.
5. Brain Tree: language/conflict analysis; consent enforcement deterministic.
6. Agent Tree: intake/preference/policy/conflict/expiry/sync/processor/evidence/QA.
7. Service Tree: record/text hash/effective/withdraw precedence/channel-purpose checks/guardian/sync/receipts/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: present exact text→capture→receipt→persist→sync→runtime enforce→withdraw/reconsent→evidence.
9. Integration Tree: web/mobile/CRM-CDP/email-SMS-push/ads/analytics/AI/warehouse/privacy.
10. Data Tree: subjects/purposes/policies/choices/receipts/processors/sync.
11. API Tree: choices/effective state/receipts/purposes/processors/sync/audit.
12. Monetization Tree: profiles/events/apps/connectors/seats/enterprise/API/packs.
13. Distribution Tree: privacy/CDP/marketing/dev/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: sync/expiry/conflict automatic; consent capture remains user-originated and policy-valid.
15. Moat Tree: processor integrations, policy packs, proof/reconciliation, conflict handling.
16. Platform Tree: preference center→consent OS→cross-system purpose enforcement.
17. Risk Tree: fabricated consent/dark patterns/stale downstream state/child consent error/privacy leak.
18. Scale Tree: app→enterprise→global processor graph.
19. Spinoff Tree: consent receipts/processor sync modules; DSAR/retention remain separate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: identity, decision/rule ledgers, policy, communications, privacy, event/outbox.
21. Design-Now Requirements: scoped owner/user decisions need purpose/effective/version/supersession/proof semantics.
22. Build-Now Requirements: keep Command Center owner preferences and future customer preferences as separate but structurally compatible ledgers.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer widgets/SDK/regional legal packs.
24. Autonomous Mature State: preferences propagate and reconcile continuously; humans/legal teams define purposes/policies while users control their own choices.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into DSAR, retention, deliverability and privacy governance already represented.

# Company 094 — Enterprise Data Lineage & Provenance Graph

**Company ID:** `company:future:094`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:094`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-094-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer-system scanning or production data mutation.

## Business identity
Purpose: map how enterprise data originates, moves, transforms and influences downstream datasets, models, agents, reports, exports and actions.

## Product tree
Source/Asset Catalog; Field/Table/Dataset Lineage; File/Document Lineage; ETL/ELT Transformation Graph; Warehouse/Lake/Lakehouse Lineage; Dashboard/BI Lineage; Model/Feature Lineage; Prompt/RAG Lineage; Agent/Decision/Action Lineage; Export/Partner Lineage; Ownership/Stewardship; Sensitivity/Policy Overlay; Freshness/Quality Overlay; Impact/Blast-Radius Analysis; Root-Cause Analysis; Change Alerts; Data Catalog; Governance; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Connector Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: node ID/type/system/owner, source-to-target edges, field mappings, transform code/version, timestamps, dataset versions, model/prompt/agent refs, sensitivity, quality, freshness, policies, consumers, downstream actions, incidents and evidence.
Customers: enterprises, data platforms, analytics/AI teams, privacy/governance, software companies, regulated organizations and data providers.
Verticals: finance data, health admin, retail/commerce, manufacturing/IoT, marketing analytics, SaaS telemetry, research/data products and agentic systems.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may explain complex lineage and infer candidate missing edges; canonical edges require observed/declared evidence. Architecture: typed graph store, connector/metadata collectors, transformation parser, schema registry, provenance event ingestion, graph versioning, sensitivity/quality overlays, impact traversal, evidence and policy integration.

## Agent tree
Source Discovery Agent; Metadata Collector; Transformation Parser; Lineage Resolver; Model/Prompt Lineage Agent; Agent/Action Lineage Agent; Ownership Agent; Sensitivity Agent; Impact Analyst; Root-Cause Agent; Drift Agent; Governance QA Agent.

## Deterministic services
Stable node/edge IDs; schema/field mapping; parser-derived transforms; event links; versioned graph snapshots; cycle/consistency checks; graph traversal; blast-radius query; change diff; provenance evidence refs.

## Workflow tree
Register systems/assets → ingest metadata/transform/event evidence → create versioned nodes/edges → validate mappings → enrich ownership/sensitivity/quality → query upstream/downstream impact → detect change/drift → alert affected owners/consumers → reconcile missing/conflicting lineage → preserve graph history.

## Integrations / API / data
Databases, warehouses, lakes, ETL/ELT, orchestration, BI, ML platforms, feature stores, AI gateways/RAG, agent systems, files/docs, APIs and data catalogs. Data: metadata/graphs/evidence rather than unnecessary raw business data.

## Monetization / distribution
Assets/nodes/edges, sources/connectors, queries, seats, enterprise/private, API and governance packs. Distribution via data/AI/governance ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Lineage metadata can expose sensitive topology. Role-scoped graph views, tenant isolation, sensitivity labels, no raw-data copying by default, secure connector credentials, immutable evidence and purpose-limited queries.

## Failure / edge cases
Dynamic SQL, opaque SaaS transformation, manual spreadsheet export, missing event, undocumented copy, derived embedding, model training snapshot, prompt assembled dynamically, cross-region replication, data deleted but lineage retained, false inferred edge. Inferred and verified lineage must be distinct.

## Scale / overlap
Data catalog → enterprise dependency graph → organization-wide provenance nervous system. Overlap #51 pipeline watchdog, #79 artifact provenance, #99 data contracts. #094 owns enterprise data dependency graph.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** stable typed lineage references across datasets/artifacts/models/agents/decisions/actions, verified-vs-inferred edges, versioned graph and sensitivity overlays.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center canonical graph should expand to represent data→Brain→Agent→decision→action lineage before factories proliferate.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer connector/graph ingestion platform.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial catalog/connector packs.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** massive federated enterprise graphs.

# Company 095 — AI ROI & Value Attribution Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:095`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:095`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-095-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no budget allocation, purchasing, staffing or financial commitment.

## Business identity
Purpose: measure whether AI models, agents and workflows create verified economic/operational value after all attributable costs, failures and human oversight.

## Product tree
AI Cost Ledger; Use-Case Registry; Baseline Builder; Outcome/Value Registry; Workflow/Agent/Model Attribution; Before/After Analysis; Experiment/A-B Support; Counterfactual/Control Analysis; Labor-Time Capacity Model; Revenue/Retention Attribution; Error/Risk Reduction; Quality/CSAT Attribution; Cycle-Time/Throughput; Failure/Support Cost; ROI/Payback/TCO; Portfolio Dashboard; Budget/Keep-Kill-Expand Recommendations; Forecast/Scenario Planning; Benchmarking; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: use case, owner, model/agent/workflow version, baseline period, comparison group, costs (model/infra/API/software/human/implementation/maintenance/failure), outcomes, attribution method/confidence, revenue/savings/capacity/risk values, time horizon, assumptions, verified vs estimated state and evidence.
Customers: enterprises, AI teams, finance/FinOps, CIO/CTO offices, agent platforms, consultancies, SaaS/AI vendors and portfolio operators.
Verticals: support, sales, engineering, finance ops, document automation, research, analytics, marketing, security and internal productivity.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may form hypotheses, explain causal uncertainty and recommend experiments; ROI arithmetic is deterministic and causal claims require explicit method/evidence. Architecture: cost/event ledger, use-case/version registry, outcome metrics, baseline/experiment store, attribution models, confidence/assumptions, financial calculator, scenario engine and audit/provenance.

## Agent tree
Cost Analyst; Baseline Agent; Outcome Agent; Attribution Analyst; Experiment Agent; Quality/Risk Agent; Forecast Agent; Portfolio Optimizer; Evidence QA Agent; Executive Brief Agent.

## Deterministic services
Cost aggregation; currency/time normalization; unit economics; ROI/payback/TCO formulas; metric definitions; baseline versioning; experiment randomization refs; confidence intervals where applicable; assumption registry; reconciliation.

## Workflow tree
Register AI use case/version → define objective/metrics/baseline → capture all costs and outcomes → choose attribution method → run experiment/control or observational analysis → calculate verified/estimated value separately → expose uncertainty → recommend keep/kill/expand/test → owner/budget authority decides → continue measurement and detect drift.

## Integrations / API / data
Model gateways, agent control center, usage billing, cloud cost, BI/data warehouse, finance/accounting, CRM/support/product analytics, HR/time systems where lawful, experimentation platforms. Data: costs, usage, outcomes, baselines, experiments, assumptions, calculations and recommendations.

## Monetization / distribution
AI spend/use cases, agents/models/workflows, seats, enterprise/private, API, benchmarking and managed value-assessment. Distribution through AI/FinOps/BI/consulting ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Avoid employee surveillance and fabricated savings. Separate capacity from actual cash savings, estimates from verified realized value, correlation from causation and revenue attribution from gross revenue. Sensitive finance/HR data isolated.

## Failure / edge cases
No stable baseline, multiple simultaneous changes, seasonality, selection bias, displaced work rather than eliminated cost, quality degradation hidden by throughput, long-term risk, human oversight shifted elsewhere, model price changes, double-counted value across agents, survivor bias.

## Scale / overlap
Use-case dashboard → enterprise AI portfolio economics → AI capital-allocation intelligence. Overlap #68 model cost routing, #69 billing, #15 BI, Command Center portfolio analytics. #095 owns value attribution.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** cost-center/use-case/model/agent/workflow IDs, actual-vs-estimate truth labels, baseline/assumption/evidence, unit economics and no-double-counting lineage.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center portfolio operations must track verified costs/value with distinct actual/estimate/forecast states before 100-company scale.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** portfolio cost/value telemetry and baseline/experiment primitives.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial customer analytics/benchmarks.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** cross-enterprise benchmarks and advanced causal models.

# Company 096 — Expense Audit & Recovery Engine

**Company ID:** `company:future:096`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:096`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-096-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no refund request, cancellation, vendor contact, payment change or financial action.

## Business identity
Purpose: continuously inspect company expenses, contracts, bills and historical charges for recoverable errors, unused credits, duplicate charges, overpayments, pricing drift and preventable future waste.

## Product tree
Expense Feed Intake; Vendor Normalization; Contract/Rate Comparison; Invoice Audit; Duplicate Charge Detection; Subscription/SaaS Audit; Cloud/Telecom/Utility Audit; Shipping/Freight Audit; Professional-Service Audit; Credit/Refund Opportunity; Overpayment Detection; Hidden Price Increase Monitor; Discount/Credit Expiry; Bank/Fee Audit; Tax Error Flagging; Expense Policy Violations; Recovery Case Manager; Savings Verification; Prevention Rules; Forecast/Benchmarking; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Managed Recovery.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: vendor/account, contract/version/rate, invoice/transaction, line item, service period, expected vs actual, duplicate fingerprint, credit/refund eligibility, price-change history, discount expiry, fee, tax, policy, confidence, recovery status and realized vs estimated savings evidence.
Customers: SMBs, enterprises, finance/procurement, accounting firms, multi-location businesses, property operators, ecommerce, SaaS-heavy companies and managed service providers.
Verticals: software/SaaS, cloud, telecom, utilities, shipping/logistics, facilities/property, professional services, advertising and general vendor spend.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may interpret contract/invoice language and propose recovery paths; deterministic contract/rate arithmetic verifies monetary discrepancies. Architecture: expense ledger, vendor/entity normalization, contract/price registry, invoice parser, anomaly/duplicate engine, expected-cost calculator, recovery case workflow, realized-savings reconciliation and evidence.

## Agent tree
Expense Intake Agent; Vendor Normalization Agent; Contract Analyst; Invoice Audit Agent; Duplicate Agent; SaaS/Subscription Agent; Utility/Telecom Agent; Shipping Agent; Recovery Case Agent; Savings Verifier; Prevention Agent; Finance QA Agent.

## Deterministic services
Line-item normalization; duplicate hashes; rate/effective-date math; contract ceilings; credit tracking; fee/tax calculations; currency; idempotent cases; realized-savings reconciliation; source/evidence hashing.

## Workflow tree
Ingest expenses/contracts → normalize vendor/service → bind exact rate/period → calculate expected cost → detect duplicate/error/credit/price drift → classify verified vs possible opportunity → finance review → protected vendor/refund/cancel workflow if authorized → reconcile actual credit/refund/avoided future charge → record realized vs estimated savings → prevention rule.

## Integrations / API / data
Accounting/ERP, cards/banks read-only, AP, contracts/CLM, SaaS spend tools, cloud billing, telecom, utilities, shipping and vendor invoices. Data: vendors/contracts/rates/invoices/transactions/credits/cases/outcomes/evidence.

## Monetization / distribution
Expense volume, vendors/accounts, subscription, percentage of verified recovered savings where appropriate, enterprise/private, API and managed recovery. Distribution via accounting/procurement/FinOps/expense ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Financial/vendor records confidential. Read-only first, deterministic evidence, no unauthorized cancellation/refund outreach, source-provenance, protected financial/vendor actions and transparent savings definitions.

## Failure / edge cases
Legitimate duplicate-looking charge, contract amendment, usage tier, prorated invoice, tax jurisdiction, currency, credit already pending, bundled invoice, annual prepaid allocation, volume discount, rate valid only for one entity, recovery fee exceeding value.

## Scale / overlap
SMB audit → enterprise spend assurance → expense recovery infrastructure. Overlap #17 SaaS spend, #43 cloud cost, #85 revenue leakage (opposite side), #48 AP verification. #096 owns paid-expense error/recovery.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** verified/estimated savings distinction, contract/rate versioning, source financial provenance, recovery case evidence and protected vendor actions.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center financial governor must separate estimated opportunity, approved action and realized savings.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer expense/contract connectors and reconciliation.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** vendor-specific recovery playbooks/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** benchmark pricing/data network.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: expense/vendor/contracts/invoice/duplicates/SaaS/cloud/telecom/utilities/shipping/services/credits/overpayments/price drift/fees/tax/recovery/API.
2. Feature Tree: vendor/contract/rate/invoice/transaction/period/expected-actual/duplicate/credit/price/discount/fee/tax/confidence/outcome.
3. Customer Tree: SMB/enterprise/finance/procurement/accounting/multi-location/property/ecommerce/MSP.
4. Vertical Tree: SaaS/cloud/telecom/utilities/shipping/property/services/ads/general spend.
5. Brain Tree: contract/invoice interpretation; money discrepancy arithmetic deterministic.
6. Agent Tree: intake/vendor/contract/invoice/duplicate/SaaS/utility/shipping/recovery/savings/prevention/QA.
7. Service Tree: normalization/hashes/rate math/ceilings/credits/fees-tax/currency/idempotency/reconcile/evidence.
8. Workflow Tree: ingest→normalize→expected cost→detect→verify→review→protected recovery→realized savings→prevent.
9. Integration Tree: accounting/cards/banks/AP/CLM/SaaS/cloud/telecom/utilities/shipping.
10. Data Tree: vendors/contracts/rates/invoices/transactions/credits/cases/outcomes/evidence.
11. API Tree: expenses/opportunities/cases/recovery/savings/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: spend/vendors/subscription/recovery share/enterprise/API/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: accounting/procurement/FinOps/expense/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: detection/verification/reconciliation automatic; vendor/refund/cancel actions gated.
15. Moat Tree: vendor pricing history, contract/rate parsers, verified recovery outcomes.
16. Platform Tree: expense audit→recovery autopilot→spend assurance infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: false recovery claim/cancel harm/contract misread/data leak/savings overstatement.
18. Scale Tree: SMB→enterprise→benchmark network.
19. Spinoff Tree: vendor benchmark/fee audit modules; SaaS/cloud optimization remain adjacent.
20. Command Center Dependencies: finance, contracts, provider/vendor identity, evidence, protected actions, analytics.
21. Design-Now Requirements: opportunities/approvals/realized savings must be distinct truth states.
22. Build-Now Requirements: Financial Governor and analytics must track expected vs verified realized economic outcomes.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer spend connectors/recovery workflows/benchmark network.
24. Autonomous Mature State: expenses are continuously audited and verified opportunities prepared; humans authorize vendor-facing recovery/cancellation and strategic changes.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into SaaS spend, cloud cost, procurement and AP products already represented.
